narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist Matthew; orderly, grave storytelling.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lord; gentle on the mountain, exasperated at unbelief, grave foretelling his Passion, quietly instructive with Peter about the tribute.

peter.name: Peter
peter.note: Apostle; awestruck on the mountain, then answering the collectors and Jesus briefly and readily.

god-the-father.name: God the Father
god-the-father.note: The voice out of the bright cloud at the Transfiguration; majestic and loving.

disciples.name: The disciples
disciples.note: Peter, James and John puzzled coming down the mountain (v10); then the disciples asking privately why they failed (v18).

father-of-possessed-boy.name: Father of the possessed boy
father-of-possessed-boy.note: A man from the multitude kneeling for his lunatic son; desperate, pleading.

didrachma-collectors.name: Collectors of the didrachma
didrachma-collectors.note: The men who collect the temple tax at Capharnaum, questioning Peter; official, slightly challenging.

1.t: And after six days Jesus taketh unto him Peter and James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into a high mountain apart:

2.t: And he was transfigured before them. And his face did shine as the sun: and his garments became white as snow.

3.t: And behold there appeared to them Moses and Elias talking with him.

4.t: And Peter answering, said to Jesus:
Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.

5.t: And as he was yet speaking, behold a bright cloud overshadowed them. And lo a voice out of the cloud, saying:
This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear ye him.

6.t: And the disciples hearing fell upon their face, and were very much afraid.

7.t: And Jesus came and touched them: and said to them:

8.t: And they lifting up their eyes, saw no one, but only Jesus.

9.t: And as they came down from the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying:
Tell the vision to no man, till the Son of man be risen from the dead.

10.t: And his disciples asked him, saying:
Why then do the scribes say that Elias must come first?
10.q: the three on the mountain (Peter, James, John), not all the disciples; kept as the group id

11.t: But he answering, said to them:
Elias indeed shall come, and restore all things.

12.t: But I say to you, that Elias is already come, and they knew him not, But have done unto him whatsoever they had a mind. So also the Son of man shall suffer from them.

13.t: Then the disciples understood, that he had spoken to them of John the Baptist.

14.t: And when he was come to the multitude, there came to him a man falling down on his knees before him saying:
Lord, have pity on my son, for he is a lunatic, and suffereth much: for he falleth often into the fire, and often into the water.

15.t: And I brought him to thy disciples, and they could not cure him.

16.t: O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I suffer you? Bring him hither to me.

17.t: And Jesus rebuked him, and the devil went out of him, and the child was cured from that hour.

18.t: Then came the disciples to Jesus secretly, and said:
Why could not we cast him out?

19.t: Because of your unbelief. For, amen I say to you, if you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you shall say to this mountain: Remove from hence hither, and it shall remove: and nothing shall be impossible to you.

20.t: But this kind is not cast out but by prayer and fasting.

21.t: And when they abode together in Galilee, Jesus said to them:
The Son of man shall be betrayed into the hands of men:

22.t: And they shall kill him, and the third day he shall rise again.

23.t: And when they were come to Capharnaum, they that received the didrachmas, came to Peter, and said to him:
Doth not your master pay the didrachma?

24.t: And when he was come into the house, Jesus prevented him, saying:
What is thy opinion, Simon? The kings of the earth, of whom do they receive tribute or custom, of their own children, or of strangers?

26.t: But that we may not scandalize them, go to the sea, and cast in a hook: and that fish which shall first come up, take: and when thou hast opened it's mouth, thou shalt find a stater: take that, and give it to them for me and thee.
